hypotheses.h0: Dispersion features add no predictive information.

payload.question: Do the dynamics of population entropy carry early-warning information about imminent search stagnation in a genetic algorithm, beyond what the fitness history already reveals, and can that signal drive a mutation intervention that recovers faster after the landscape changes?

spec.rationale: H1 is the core question (entropy beyond fitness history). Development LOLO on rastrigin+ackley, 15 seeds. If AUROC gain is clearly positive, H1 gains and justifies a held-out confirmation and use in H4's controller; if ~0, entropy likely adds nothing and H4 loses its premise.
spec.title: Dev: entropy features vs fitness-only (H1)

spec.rationale: Tests two rival signals in one run (H2 genotypic dispersion, H3 genotype-free fitness spread), 12 seeds on dev landscapes. If spread helps as much as entropy, a cheaper genotype-free signal suffices; if neither helps, the information claim narrows to entropy. Efficient coverage of two uncertain hypotheses.
spec.title: Dev: fitness-spread vs dispersion vs fitness-only (H2,H3)

spec.rationale: Directly tests the intervention claim on dev landscapes, 8 seeds, against B0_fixed and the stall/entropy baselines. If B3 shortens recovery time, the signal is actionable; if not, even a valid predictor does not translate to control, redirecting effort to the prediction hypotheses.
spec.title: Dev: B3 predictive controller recovery time (H4)

payload.justification: E2 is the utility argmax (0.6725 vs E1 0.834 utility; EIG 1.6766 bits vs 0.8383 for E1 and 0.3483 for E3). It tests H2 and H3 together, at an estimated cost of 2.44 s and feasible with no violations. Per-hypothesis power equals E1's (0.97), so the lead comes from covering two hypotheses. The result would move the posteriors for H2 and H3, and it shows whether dispersion or fitness-spread features beat fitness history alone. E1, which tests the central entropy question, is the next candidate.

payload.interpretation:
RESULT (development stage, leave-one-landscape-out, n_units=72 runs, 5188 test points, stagnation prevalence 0.028). AUROC: fitness 0.677 [0.615, 0.7381]; fitness+dispersion 0.7076 [0.6523, 0.7627]; fitness+spread 0.6851 [0.6256, 0.7447]. Delta AUROC vs fitness: dispersion +0.0306 [0.0213, 0.0407] (standardised 0.719); spread +0.0081 [-0.0073, 0.0231] (standardised 0.122). Brier: 0.0272 / 0.0271 / 0.0271, i.e. no calibration gain.

INTERPRETATION. H2: the dispersion gain is about 3x the 0.01 smallest effect of interest, and the whole CI lies above 0.01 (lower bound 0.0213). It is a real but modest discrimination gain, and the absolute AUROC of 0.71 is still weak. H3: inconclusive. The point estimate 0.0081 is below the 0.01 SESOI, and the CI [-0.0073, 0.0231] spans both zero and the SESOI, so neither a useful effect nor a null can be claimed. This is not evidence of absence.

Cheaper-signal note: dispersion (genotype access) helps; fitness-spread (cheaper, no genotype needed) does not clearly help. Entropy (H1) was not tested here. E1 is needed to see whether entropy beats dispersion. If it does not, the entropy narrative is undercut, since dispersion is the cheaper and simpler genotypic signal.

The Brier scores are identical to 3 decimals. With 2.8% prevalence, ranking improved but probabilities did not, so the gain may not matter for a threshold-based controller (H4).
threats_to_validity: Development-stage result: the landscapes are the dev set and results are typically optimistic. A held-out confirmation run is needed before this counts as confirmatory.

Low base rate (2.8%) means few positive events. Positives are clustered within runs, so the effective sample size is closer to 72 runs than 5188 points. Check that the CIs resample at the run/landscape level, not the point level.
Leave-one-landscape-out across a small number of landscapes: distribution shift between landscapes could drive the dispersion gain, and per-landscape heterogeneity is not shown.
Brier is unchanged, so there is no calibration benefit. A discrimination gain of +0.0306 AUROC may not translate to better control decisions in H4.
Multiple comparisons (H1-H3 across E1/E2) are not corrected, and the entropy features in H1 are not compared against dispersion, so the lab's core entropy claim is untested.
Dispersion and entropy are likely correlated, and the DISP gain may be leakage-adjacent if the stagnation label is defined by population convergence (label definition overlaps with the feature).

payload.h0: Delta AUROC (fitness+dispersion+entropy minus fitness+dispersion) is below 0.01 (entropy adds nothing beyond dispersion).
payload.statement: [agent-generated] Adding population-entropy features (H_t, dH_t) to fitness+dispersion features improves out-of-sample AUROC by at least 0.01, i.e. entropy carries information beyond the cheaper dispersion signal.

payload.decision: Treat dispersion as a supported early-warning feature (development stage only). Next, test whether entropy adds anything: H1 directly, and H5 (entropy beyond dispersion).
payload.rationale: E2: H2 posterior 0.5 -> 0.975 (supported; delta AUROC 0.0306 [0.0213, 0.0407]). H3 posterior 0.5 -> 0.667 but the verdict is inconclusive (delta 0.0081 [-0.0073, 0.0231]); the rise comes from the update rule and is not support. Brier did not improve (0.0272 vs 0.0271), so ranking gains may not help a controller. The critic flagged that the CIs may not account for clustering within runs. The central entropy question (H1, 0.5) is still untested, and the critic registered H5 (agent-generated) to ask whether entropy adds anything beyond dispersion. The result reopens the assumption that entropy is the key signal. Next round: ask the designer for candidates covering H1 and H5 and for E3 to include hypermutation and random-immigrant baselines.

spec.rationale: Compares restricted mean recovery time after landscape shifts for B3_predictive against B0_fixed, B1_stall, B2_entropy, B4a_hypermutation and B4b_immigrants, 12 seeds on development landscapes. If B3 beats the strongest non-oracle baseline (incl. hypermutation/immigrants): H4 supported and the predictor is operationally useful. If it only matches them: ranking gains (AUROC, no Brier gain) do not translate into control, so the predictor adds no value over simple triggers. If it loses: drop the predictive controller.
spec.title: Dev: B3 predictive vs hypermutation and random-immigrant baselines (H4)

spec.rationale: Cheaper 8-seed control run with B0_fixed, B3_predictive, B4a_hypermutation, B4b_immigrants only (omits B1/B2). Competes on size and baseline breadth: faster, but cannot say whether B3 beats stall/entropy triggers. If B3 clearly beats both dynamic-environment baselines it justifies the fuller run; if not, we save compute.
spec.title: Dev (lean): B3 vs hypermutation/immigrants only (H4)

spec.rationale: Tests H1 only (fitness+entropy vs fitness), also including fitness+dispersion for reference, 16 seeds on development landscapes. If supported: entropy carries signal beyond fitness history, motivating a confirmatory run and the H5 follow-up. If not: the central entropy premise is undermined, and dispersion remains the working signal. H5 cannot be registered here because the design space has no fitness+dispersion+entropy set ('full' also adds spread).
spec.title: Dev: entropy vs fitness-only (H1), 16 seeds

payload.justification: E4 is the utility argmax (utility 0.4826, EIG 0.4903 bits, est. cost 4.6 s, feasible with no violations). It tests H4 against hypermutation and random-immigrant baselines, which the critic asked for. H4 is the lab's only control hypothesis and is untested. The H1 candidates (E6 EIG 0.137, E1 EIG 0.1274) have low power at the small assumed effect size, and H5 could not be built from the current feature sets, so I did not override. The result could confirm or refute that a frozen risk model drives faster recovery than the strongest non-oracle baseline. H1 and H5 stay open and will need a new feature set or a proxy.

payload.interpretation: RESULT (development stage, n_units=24, 120 paired runs): B3_predictive vs strongest non-oracle baseline (B0_fixed) reduces RMST by 0.2583 generations (95% CI [-3.1088, 3.325]); standardised effect 0.031. B3 RMST 51.67 vs B0 51.93. Verdict: inconclusive. The CI spans zero and is roughly +/-3 gens, i.e. it cannot exclude a 1-generation benefit or a 3-generation harm; the point estimate is far below the 1-generation smallest effect of interest. B3 recovery rate 0.6083 [0.5189, 0.691] vs B0 0.5167 [0.4281, 0.6042]: overlapping CIs. Rescue/damage vs B0: 29 rescued, 18 damaged (McNemar p=0.1439, not significant). CVaR90 is 60.0 gens for every controller, so the tail is censored at the horizon and uninformative. Other comparisons: B4a hypermutation delta RMST +2.6833 [-0.2417, 5.5085] (no better than fixed, not rejected); B4b immigrants +5.575 [2.9667, 8.3333] (worse, Holm reject); B1_stall +3.5667 [0.2917, 6.7754] (worse, not Holm-rejected); B2_entropy +7.4917 [4.7831, 10.1921] (much worse, Holm reject; 61 damaged vs 1 rescued, recovery 0.0167 [0.0046, 0.0587]). INTERPRETATION: No adaptive controller beat fixed mutation at p=0.1, so the literature baselines (hypermutation, immigrants) are not beaten by B3 in a meaningful sense, and B3 only matches the do-nothing control. The direct entropy-threshold controller (B2) is actively harmful (mean p_mut 0.2649), which does not support entropy as a cheap actionable signal. B3 mean p_mut is 0.0811, below the fixed 0.1, so any trend toward benefit may come from simply lowering mutation rather than from predictive timing; this is not separable here. H4 is not supported; the direction is neutral.
threats_to_validity: Underpowered: 24 units, CI half-width about 3.2 gens vs a 1-gen SESOI; the null is not evidence of no effect. Development stage only, results can be optimistic and not confirmatory.

Unit of analysis / clustering: 120 paired runs from 24 units (landscape/seed); McNemar and recovery-rate CIs treat runs as independent, which likely understates uncertainty. Also 6 controllers compared with Holm; B3 'no effect' is not corrected-significant either way.

Confound: B3 lowers mean p_mut (0.0811 vs 0.1), so the predictive controller is not distinguished from a simply lower fixed mutation rate; no matched fixed-rate control (e.g. p_mut=0.08) is included. Also B0 at 0.1 may be miscalibrated for these landscapes.

Risk model is fit on only 72 runs with fitness+entropy features (entropy coefficient 0.536), and E2 found dispersion, not entropy, as the supported signal (Brier unchanged); the risk model may not transfer to post-shift dynamics or to the 2 eps landscapes (ackley, rastrigin) with different scales; distribution shift between landscapes is untested.
Censoring: recovery cap at 60 gens, CVaR90 = 60 for all controllers, recovery rates of 0.02-0.61 mean RMST is dominated by the cap and compresses differences.

payload.h0: B3 RMST reduction vs a fixed p_mut=0.08 control is below 1 generation (no benefit from predictive timing).
payload.statement: [agent-generated] The B3 predictive controller lowers RMST after landscape shifts versus a fixed-mutation control whose rate is matched to B3's mean p_mut (about 0.08), i.e. its timing carries benefit beyond simply mutating less.

payload.decision: Do not claim a control benefit. Next, run a larger confirmatory-style test of H6 (B3 vs a rate-matched fixed p_mut of about 0.08) and a B3 variant driven by dispersion, with run-clustered analysis. H5 needs a new feature set (fitness+dispersion+entropy), which the planner cannot currently build.
payload.next_experiment: H6 test: B3 vs matched fixed p_mut=0.08, plus dispersion-driven B3
payload.rationale: E4: H4 is inconclusive. B3 vs B0_fixed delta RMST is -0.2583 gens, 95% CI [-3.325, 3.1088]. The critic's update reports H4 at 0.3 -> 0.3036; the state shows 0.304 (the state showed 0.5 before E4, so the 0.3 base is a tool prior and I report both). The entropy-threshold controller B2 was clearly harmful (+7.4917 [4.7831, 10.1921]), so entropy did not beat cheaper signals as a controller trigger. B3's mean p_mut is 0.0811 vs 0.1, so timing is confounded with a lower rate (H6, agent-generated, 0.5). This reopens the assumption that entropy is the useful signal: E2 supported dispersion (H2 0.975) while the B3 risk model used fitness+entropy. H1 and H5 remain untested (0.5 each).
